title: Identity normalization of the underived open exchange
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], let $j:U\to T$ be an open immersion, and let $sq$ be an open-immersion square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square] with horizontal maps $1_U,1_T$ and vertical maps $j,j$. Let $F_X$ be the completed module pullback along $1_X$ and $J$ the ordinary module extension by zero of [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison]. Define $u_X:F_X\cong1$ by the equality cbcDatumModulePull_eq followed by the left-adjoint identity isomorphism of the section-normalized ordinary adjunction and modulePushId of [lem-weil-pbc-completed-ordinary-comparisons]. For every completed-coefficient module $M$ on $U$, the underived inverse exchange $b_M:J(F_U M)\to F_T(JM)$ satisfies $b_M\,u_T(JM)=J(u_U(M))$. This is an equality of module morphisms before passing to complexes or derived categories; no quasi-compactness or completeness assumption is imposed.

source.place: lemma-shriek-base-change, identity specialization; sites-modules.tex, lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-sites and lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules.

proof.text: Compare cbcCompletedModuleDirectImage with the datum module direct image. Their coefficient maps are adjoints of completedCoefficientMap and integralRingIso.hom, equal by cbcDatumCoefficient_eq. The module pullback equality is cbcDatumModulePull_eq. Transport the datum module adjunction through these equalities: its unit on the small model sends x to the same sheafified tensor 1 tensor x. The tensor/sheafification normalization in cbcModulePullbackAdjunction_exists identifies it with the recorded completed-module adjunction. Thus its left-adjoint identity is exactly u_X.

For a module N on T and a test object V over U, use the section formula of cbcRightExchange_exists. Its restriction is along the canonical comparison V times_U U to V times_T T. Follow with the direct-image identity on U, or first use the direct-image identity on T and then restrict to U. These section maps coincide: their underlying maps from V to V times_T T both have first projection the identity and second projection V to U to T. Pullback extensionality and functoriality of N restriction prove the equality, including for an empty V. Finite coefficient projection equalities ensure the same completed scalar action.

Take the inverse conjugate under the two composite adjunctions defining cbcUnderivedInverseExchange. Conjugation respects composition and whiskering. The two direct-image identities transpose to u_U and u_T by leftAdjointIdIso. Cancel the intermediate open-adjunction unit and counit using the triangle identities. This gives b_M followed by u_T(JM) equals J(u_U(M)). The proof is entirely in module categories and has no derived or K-flat input.

lean.statement:
theorem cbcUnderivedInverseExchange_identity
    {A : Type (t + 1)} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A)
    {U T : Scheme.{t}} (j : U ⟶ T) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (sq : OpenImmersionSquare (𝟙 U) j j (𝟙 T))
    (M : pbcModules U (pbcAdicCompletion U d)) :
    (cbcUnderivedInverseExchange d sq).app M ≫
        (cbcModulePullId d T).hom.app ((cbcOpenShriek d j inferInstance).obj M) =
      (cbcOpenShriek d j inferInstance).map ((cbcModulePullId d U).hom.app M)
